title: Velocity of Points on Rigid Links
subtitle: This week introduces kinematics — the study of motion without caring about forces. You'll learn how to find the velocity of any point on a moving link using equations and graphical methods. This is the starting point for everything in mechanisms.
learningOutcome: This week introduces kinematics — the study of motion without caring about forces. You'll learn how to find the velocity of any point on a moving link using equations and graphical methods. This is the starting point for everything in mechanisms.

content.text: Kinematics is the study of motion. It doesn't ask "why is it moving?" — it only asks "how is it moving?". Think of it like watching a car from above: you can see it speeding up, slowing down, turning — but you don't know or care about the engine inside.

Velocity is a characteristic of kinematics. When a rigid link rotates, every single point on it moves — but they all move at different speeds depending on how far they are from the centre of rotation.
v = final velocity (m/s) · u = initial velocity (m/s) · a = acceleration (m/s²) · t = time (s) · s = displacement (m)
Velocity of a point on a rotating link
V_A = velocity of point A (m/s) · O₁A = distance from centre of rotation to point A (m) · ω₂ = angular velocity of the link (rad/s)

content.caption: Rotating link — velocity of a point
content.description: O₁ (fixed) · A · V_A = ω × O₁A · r = O₁A · ω₂ · V always acts perpendicular to the link

content.text: Think of a ceiling fan. The centre (O₁) is fixed to the ceiling. Each blade tip is like point A. The longer the blade, the faster that tip moves — even though the whole fan rotates at the same ω. That's exactly what V_A = ω × r tells you.
Common mistake — Students forget that V acts perpendicular to the link , not along it. If you draw your velocity arrow pointing along the rod, that's wrong. It must be at 90° to the link direction.

items: • State the equations of motion for constant acceleration and use them to find velocity or displacement.
• Define velocity and state that it is a characteristic of kinematics.
• Given a mechanism, find the velocity of a point using V = ω × r.
